descriptionChirho: The abstract noun denoting deception, treachery, or fraudulence as an activity or quality — the act of deceiving or the state of being deceptive. Used substantively (e.g., 'a tongue of deceit,' 'balances of deceit'): eng deceit, spa engaño, hin छल, arb غِشّ, kor 속임-을, swa udanganyifu. Across all languages the translations point to the noun concept of deception or fraud as an abstract condition.

The same noun used attributively or predicatively to characterize something as deceitful, slack, or treacherous — functioning almost as an adjective. Translations shift from abstract noun to descriptive quality: eng deceitful (vs. deceit), spa engañoso (adjectival -oso suffix), hin धोखेबाज (agent/quality suffix -बाज), arb مُرتَخٍ (slack/lax participle), kor 속이는 (verbal adjective), swa wa-uongo (possessive 'of falsehood'). The multilingual evidence clearly distinguishes this attributive usage from the pure abstract noun.
